selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What is presented as the beginning of every good action?
questions.answer: Saying Allah’s name at the start.

questions.question: What does the passage say this phrase is for Islam?
questions.answer: It is one of its clear signs.

questions.question: What was the main difference between the two men who entered the desert?
questions.answer: One was humble and accepted protection, while the other was proud and refused it.

questions.question: Why would a person be in great danger there without protection?
questions.answer: He would face attacks and many needs by himself.

questions.question: What happened to the proud man during the journey?
questions.answer: He faced many troubles, became afraid, begged from others, and was looked down on.

questions.question: What was the result for the first traveler?
questions.answer: He traveled safely and was treated well.

questions.question: Why should a person take the name of Allah according to the passage?
questions.answer: So he will not fear everything or lower himself by begging from all creation.

questions.question: What does taking Allah’s name save a person from?
questions.answer: From fear of events and from depending on everything else.

questions.question: What example is given to explain a person who acts in Allah’s name?
questions.answer: A person enrolled in the army who acts with the authority of the government.

questions.question: What big message ties the story and the final example together?
questions.answer: Relying on Allah brings protection and honor, while trusting only yourself leads to trouble.

questions.question: What special phrase is the passage explaining?
questions.answer: The phrase that means beginning in Allah’s name.

questions.question: What does the passage say all creatures do in their own way?
questions.answer: They point to and declare Allah’s name through how they were made.

questions.question: Why is the desert journey dangerous for someone traveling alone?
questions.answer: Because there are many threats and many needs he cannot handle by himself.

questions.question: What personal quality helped the first man make a good choice?
questions.answer: Humility.

questions.question: What mistake did the proud man make?
questions.answer: He trusted himself and refused protection.

questions.question: How did it help him with ordinary people in the tents?
questions.answer: It caused them to welcome and honor him.

questions.question: What feeling can a person leave behind by beginning in Allah’s name?
questions.answer: Constant fear.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about human ability on its own?
questions.answer: It is not enough because people are very weak and needy.

questions.question: Why is joining the army a good example here?
questions.answer: Because the soldier has backing, authority, and courage beyond his own strength.

questions.question: What should Muslims begin with according to the passage?
questions.answer: They should begin with Allah’s name.

questions.question: How does the passage describe this phrase at the beginning?
questions.answer: As the proper start of every good matter.

questions.question: What does a traveler gain by entering under a chief’s protection?
questions.answer: Safety and help in meeting his needs.

questions.question: What did travelers in that setting need from a tribal leader?
questions.answer: His name and protection.

questions.question: What happened to the humble traveler when he used the chief’s name?
questions.answer: People did not harm him, and he received respect.
